editions.headline: Minimum wage rises to $16.50 in Calder
editions.text: Calder's minimum wage rose to $16.50 an hour on Jan. 1, up 50 cents under the state's inflation adjustment. Tipped workers receive the same minimum.

editions.headline: Snowpack at 51% of average in January survey
editions.text: Surveyors measured the Calder snowpack at 51% of the long-term average for Jan. 2, the Department of Water Resources said. Officials asked cities to plan for a dry summer.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Puerto Claro aprueba la ampliación de la costanera
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 2 de enero por 11 votos contra 1. Las obras comenzarían el año próximo.

editions.headline: Employers added 104,000 jobs in December; unemployment falls to 4%
editions.text: Employers added 104,000 jobs in December, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate fell to 4%. Average hourly pay rose 0.3% from the month before. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: Unemployment down at 4% in December
editions.text: Employers added 104,000 jobs in December, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate fell to 4%. Average hourly pay rose 0.3% from the month before. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: Frost advisory for low-lying parts of Valley County
editions.text: Temperatures could fall to 29 degrees around Alder Creek and Riverside before sunrise on Sunday, Jan. 5. The weather service advised covering sensitive plants and bringing pets inside.

editions.headline: El puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 19 cruceros en diciembre
editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 33,288 pasajeros de 19 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante diciembre. Los comerciantes del casco histórico reportaron más ventas que en la temporada anterior.

editions.headline: Stamp price rises to 71 cents on Jan. 19
editions.text: A first-class stamp will cost 71 cents starting Jan. 19, up from 68 cents, the Postal Service reminded customers Tuesday. Forever stamps bought earlier remain valid.

editions.headline: Millbrook approves 205-unit apartment building on Elm Street
editions.text: The Millbrook City Council voted 4-2 to approve the project, 11% of whose units will rent below market rate. Neighbors had asked for a shorter building. The council met Tuesday, Jan. 7.

editions.headline: El Concejo de San Telmo aprueba la peatonalización de la calle Mitre
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 9 de enero por 11 votos contra 1. Los vecinos podrán presentar objeciones durante 30 días.

editions.headline: Comienza la temporada de calamar en Punta Brava
editions.text: La flota artesanal de Punta Brava salió el viernes 10 de enero para la apertura de la temporada de calamar. La cooperativa de pescadores espera capturas similares a las del año pasado, aunque el combustible subió un 8% desde 2024.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el martes en Bahía Honda
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el martes 14 de enero de 22 a 6 horas entre las calles Alsina y Rivadavia de Bahía Honda, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 62 km/h para el miércoles
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 92 km/h para el miércoles 15 de enero. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre San Telmo y Villa Marina, y recomendó asegurar toldos y carteles.

editions.headline: Transit agency proposes first Valley Line fare increase since 2019
editions.text: Valley Regional Transit staff have proposed raising the base Valley Line fare from $2.50 to $2.75 on July 1, the first increase since 2019. Monthly passes would rise from $80 to $88. The board will hold a public hearing Feb. 11 at the Millbrook headquarters; written comments are due Feb. 7.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 92 km/h para el jueves
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 93 km/h para el jueves 16 de enero. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre Bahía Honda y Villa Marina, y el puerto demoró la salida de dos buques de carga.

editions.headline: Valley Unified weighs closing Pine Hollow Elementary
editions.text: Valley Unified trustees will study closing Pine Hollow Elementary, where enrollment has fallen to 140 students. A decision is expected in March.

editions.headline: Prices up 2.9% from a year earlier in December
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 2.9% in the year to December, the same as 2.9% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Airfares dropped after the summer peak.

editions.headline: Reserve Council holds key rate at 4.5%
editions.text: The Reserve Council left its benchmark rate at 4.5% at the end of its January meeting on Wednesday, Jan. 15. Governor Elaine Marchetti said inflation was easing more slowly than expected.

editions.headline: El Concejo de San Telmo aprueba la ampliación de la costanera
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 16 de enero por 10 votos contra 2. Las obras comenzarían el año próximo.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment dips to 5.1% in December
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate fell to 5.1% in December, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers added 6,500 jobs; state and local government led the change.

editions.headline: Millbrook to repave 12 streets this summer
editions.text: The Millbrook City Council approved a $3,080,000 contract to repave 12 streets, starting with Pacific Avenue and Elm Street. The city will post a street-by-street schedule online; residents will get door hangers 72 hours before work. The council met Tuesday, Jan. 21.

editions.headline: Eastbank budget adds 5 firefighters
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council adopted a $119 million budget that adds firefighters and extends library hours. Mayor Hollis Grant called it "a careful budget in an uncertain year." The council met Tuesday, Jan. 21.

editions.headline: Harbor City approves new playground for Bayview Park
editions.text: The Harbor City Council voted 4-1 to spend $760,000 on a new playground at Bayview Park, with construction starting in the fall. A parent group raised $40,000 toward the cost. The council met Tuesday, Jan. 21.

editions.headline: Bill would raise the state minimum wage to $18 by 2027
editions.text: Sen. Paula Reyes introduced SB 301 on Thursday, a bill that would raise the state minimum wage to $18 by 2027. Supporters include several county governments.

editions.headline: Storm to bring 1 inches of rain to the valley
editions.text: A Pacific storm will reach Valley County on the night of Friday, Jan. 24, with 2 inches of rain expected by Sunday. Snow levels will drop to 4,000 feet in the eastern foothills. Highs will stay near 61.

editions.headline: Bill would require metering of large agricultural wells
editions.text: Assemblymember Nadia Farouk introduced AB 406 on Saturday, a bill that would require metering of large agricultural wells. A similar bill died in committee two years ago.

editions.headline: Bakery opens on Millbrook's Mill Road
editions.text: Grace Muñoz opened a bakery in Millbrook on Sunday, in a space that had been empty since 2024. The owner said she had saved for six years to open it.

editions.headline: Bill would speed up permits for homes near transit
editions.text: Assemblymember June Halvorsen introduced SB 112 on Tuesday, a bill that would speed up permits for homes near transit. Supporters include several county governments.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 92 km/h para el viernes
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 75 km/h para el viernes 31 de enero. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre Punta Brava y Villa Marina. Las clases continúan con normalidad.

editions.headline: Economy grew at 2.3% rate in fourth quarter
editions.text: The economy grew at a 2.3% annual rate in the fourth quarter of 2024, the Commerce Office said Thursday. Consumer spending accounted for most of the growth.

editions.headline: El Concejo de San Telmo aprueba una tasa turística
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 30 de enero por 9 votos contra 3. Los comerciantes pidieron una etapa de prueba de seis meses.

editions.headline: Bill would limit insurer cancellations in high fire-risk areas
editions.text: Sen. Paula Reyes introduced SB 58 on Friday, a bill that would limit insurer cancellations in high fire-risk areas. The governor's office has not taken a position.

editions.headline: Snowpack at 82% of average in February survey
editions.text: Surveyors measured the Calder snowpack at 82% of the long-term average for Feb. 1, the Department of Water Resources said. Reservoirs are near normal for the date.

editions.headline: El puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 19 cruceros en enero
editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 28,424 pasajeros de 19 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante enero. Los comerciantes del casco histórico reportaron más ventas que en la temporada anterior.

editions.headline: Harbor City approves 178-unit apartment building near the station
editions.text: The Harbor City Council voted 5-1 to approve the project, 15% of whose units will rent below market rate. Neighbors had asked for a shorter building. The council met Tuesday, Feb. 4.

editions.headline: Millbrook names new fire chief
editions.text: The Millbrook City Council confirmed Imani Brooks, a 20-year veteran of the department, as fire chief. Mayor Denise Arceo praised the choice. The council met Tuesday, Feb. 4.

editions.headline: Lantern Festival lights up the waterfront Saturday
editions.text: The Harbor City Lantern Festival returns to the waterfront Feb. 8-9, with 1185 lanterns made by schools and neighborhood groups. Pier Park lots open at 4 p.m.; parking is $10.

editions.headline: Bakery opens on Pine Hollow's Station Way
editions.text: Tariq Haddad opened a bakery in Pine Hollow on Wednesday, in a space that had been empty since 2022. Hours are 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., Tuesday through Sunday.

editions.headline: Storm to bring 2 inches of rain to the valley
editions.text: A Pacific storm will reach Valley County on the night of Thursday, Feb. 6, with 2 inches of rain expected by Saturday. Snow levels will drop to 4,000 feet in the eastern foothills. Highs will stay near 59.

editions.headline: Employers added 138,000 jobs in January; unemployment holds at 4%
editions.text: Employers added 138,000 jobs in January, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate held at 4%. Average hourly pay rose 0.3% from the month before. Economists had expected a smaller change.

editions.headline: Bill would set an age limit of 14 for riding e-bikes
editions.text: Assemblymember Chris Lyle introduced SB 260 on Friday, a bill that would set an age limit of 14 for riding e-bikes. Supporters include several county governments.

editions.headline: Riders crowd hearing on proposed Valley Line fare increase
editions.text: About 90 riders spoke at Tuesday night's Valley Regional Transit hearing on a 25-cent fare increase, most of them asking the board to keep the monthly pass at $80. Several Alder Creek riders said trains already run too rarely after 8 p.m. The board will vote March 11.

editions.headline: Winter storm closes interstates across the northern plains
editions.text: Blowing snow closed more than 400 miles of interstate across three northern states on Wednesday, stranding hundreds of trucks. Forecasters expect wind chills near 40 below.

editions.headline: Prices up 2.8% from a year earlier in January
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 2.8% in the year to January, down from 2.9% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Airfares dropped after the summer peak.

editions.headline: Plant nursery opens on Riverside's Mill Road
editions.text: Maya Lindgren opened a plant nursery in Riverside on Friday, in a space that had been empty since 2021. Hours are 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., Tuesday through Sunday.

editions.headline: El Festival de la Corvina reunió a 19,000 personas en Bahía Honda
editions.text: La trigésima edición del festival reunió a unas 19,000 personas durante el fin de semana en Bahía Honda. Hubo concursos de pesca, música en vivo y puestos de comida de toda la Costa Norte; el premio mayor fue una corvina de 7,4 kilos.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Tuesday, Feb. 18. Fog is expected again Wednesday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 54.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 72 km/h para el jueves
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 84 km/h para el jueves 20 de febrero. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre San Telmo y Villa Marina, y el puerto demoró la salida de dos buques de carga.

editions.headline: Eastbank City Council delays vote on downtown parking meters
editions.text: After two hours of public comment on downtown parking meters, the Eastbank City Council postponed its vote to next month and asked staff to meet with landlords. 61 people signed up to speak. The council met Tuesday, Feb. 18.

editions.headline: Millbrook approves skate park for Bayview Park
editions.text: The Millbrook City Council voted 4-1 to spend $920,000 on a skate park at Bayview Park, with construction starting in the fall. Neighbors asked the city to keep the existing trees. The council met Tuesday, Feb. 18.

editions.headline: Harbor City names new parks director
editions.text: The Harbor City Council confirmed Lorraine Fisk, formerly of Cinder Bay, as parks director. Mayor Victor Lam praised the choice. The council met Tuesday, Feb. 18.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment holds at 5.1% in January
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate held at 5.1% in January, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers cut 6,500 jobs; leisure and hospitality was the only sector to shrink.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Saturday, Feb. 22. Fog is expected again Sunday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 49.

editions.headline: Taqueria opens on Eastbank's Main Street
editions.text: Lucy Fontaine opened a taqueria in Eastbank on Sunday, in a space that had been empty since 2024. It is the third new business on the block this year.

editions.headline: Comienza la temporada de merluza en Puerto Claro
editions.text: La flota artesanal de Puerto Claro salió el sábado 1 de marzo para la apertura de la temporada de merluza. La cooperativa de pescadores espera capturas similares a las del año pasado, aunque el combustible subió un 6% desde 2024.

editions.headline: AB 406 clears first committee
editions.text: A Calder Senate committee voted 7-4 on Saturday to advance AB 406, which would require metering of large agricultural wells. Amendments narrowed the bill to larger counties.

editions.headline: Snowpack at 74% of average in March survey
editions.text: Surveyors measured the Calder snowpack at 74% of the long-term average for March 2, the Department of Water Resources said. Reservoirs are near normal for the date.

editions.headline: La línea 7 de colectivos cambia su frecuencia
editions.text: Desde el 10 de marzo, la línea 7 entre Puerto Claro y San Telmo pasará cada 16 minutos en hora pico. La empresa sumará 5 unidades con aire acondicionado.

editions.headline: El puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 20 cruceros en febrero
editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 37,400 pasajeros de 20 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante febrero. Los comerciantes del casco histórico reportaron más ventas que en la temporada anterior.

editions.headline: Harbor City water rates to rise 7% in July
editions.text: The Harbor City Council approved a 7% water rate increase to pay for pipe replacement. A typical household will pay about $6.90 more a month. Some mains under Oak Street date to the 1940s, staff said. The council met Tuesday, March 4.

editions.headline: Plant nursery opens on Riverside's Mill Road
editions.text: Grace Muñoz opened a plant nursery in Riverside on Wednesday, in a space that had been empty since 2022. Hours are 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., Tuesday through Sunday.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 90 km/h para el viernes
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 72 km/h para el viernes 7 de marzo. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre Bahía Honda y Punta Brava, y el puerto demoró la salida de dos buques de carga.

editions.headline: SB 58 clears first committee
editions.text: A Calder Assembly committee voted 8-4 on Thursday to advance SB 58, which would limit insurer cancellations in high fire-risk areas. Opponents said the cost estimate was too low.

editions.headline: Employers added 30,000 jobs in February; unemployment falls to 3.9%
editions.text: Employers added 30,000 jobs in February, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate fell to 3.9%. Health care and construction led the gains. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: Unemployment down at 3.9% in February

editions.headline: SB 112 clears first committee
editions.text: A Calder Senate committee voted 6-2 on Sunday to advance SB 112, which would speed up permits for homes near transit. Amendments narrowed the bill to larger counties.

editions.headline: Valley transit board raises fare to $2.75, keeps monthly pass at $84
editions.text: The Valley Regional Transit board voted 5-2 on Tuesday to raise the base Valley Line fare to $2.75 on July 1. After a hearing in which riders objected to the pass increase, the board set the monthly pass at $84 instead of the proposed $88. Reduced fares for seniors and students stay at $1.25.

editions.headline: Trustees keep Pine Hollow Elementary open for now
editions.text: The Valley Unified board voted 4-1 to keep Pine Hollow Elementary open through at least June 2027 while it tries a dual-language program to attract families.

editions.headline: Prices up 2.7% from a year earlier in February
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 2.7% in the year to February, down from 2.8% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Grocery prices rose 0.4% in the month alone.

editions.headline: SB 301 clears first committee
editions.text: A Calder Assembly committee voted 9-2 on Monday to advance SB 301, which would raise the state minimum wage to $18 by 2027. Opponents said the cost estimate was too low.

editions.headline: Eastbank to repave 8 streets this summer
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council approved a $2,230,000 contract to repave 8 streets, starting with Harbor Boulevard and Oak Street. The city will post a street-by-street schedule online; residents will get door hangers 72 hours before work. The council met Tuesday, March 18.

editions.headline: Reserve Council holds key rate at 4.5%
editions.text: The Reserve Council left its benchmark rate at 4.5% at the end of its March meeting on Wednesday, March 19. Governor Elaine Marchetti said inflation was easing more slowly than expected.

editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 20 de marzo por 10 votos contra 3. Las obras comenzarían el año próximo.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment rises to 5.2% in February
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate rose to 5.2% in February, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers cut 2,500 jobs; leisure and hospitality was the only sector to shrink.

editions.text: A Calder Assembly committee voted 6-2 on Friday to advance SB 260, which would set an age limit of 14 for riding e-bikes. Amendments narrowed the bill to larger counties.

editions.headline: Used-record store opens on Riverside's Front Street
editions.text: Ben Achebe opened a used-record store in Riverside on Sunday, in a space that had been empty since 2023. The owner said she had saved for six years to open it.

editions.headline: Storm to bring 2 inches of rain to the valley
editions.text: A Pacific storm will reach Valley County on the night of Monday, March 24, with 2 inches of rain expected by Wednesday. Snow levels will drop to 3,000 feet in the eastern foothills. Highs will stay near 58.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el sábado en Punta Brava
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el sábado 29 de marzo de 8 a 14 horas entre las calles Rivadavia y Moreno de Punta Brava, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: Puerto Claro inaugura una nueva sala de atención primaria
editions.text: El centro de salud de Puerto Claro abrirá de lunes a sábado de 8 a 20 horas y tendrá 5 consultorios. La municipalidad invirtió 354 millones de pesos en la obra, que comenzó en 2024.

editions.headline: Frost advisory for low-lying parts of Valley County
editions.text: Temperatures could fall to 28 degrees around Alder Creek and Riverside before sunrise on Sunday, March 30. The weather service advised covering sensitive plants and bringing pets inside.

editions.headline: Senate passes AB 406
editions.text: The Assembly passed AB 406 23-16 on Tuesday. The bill would require metering of large agricultural wells. It now goes to the other chamber.

editions.headline: Snowpack at 99% of average in season-ending survey
editions.text: Surveyors measured the Calder snowpack at 99% of the long-term average for April 1, the Department of Water Resources said. Reservoirs are near normal for the date.

editions.headline: Eastbank approves 61-unit apartment building near the station
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council voted 5-1 to approve the project, 12% of whose units will rent below market rate. Neighbors had asked for a shorter building. The council met Tuesday, April 1.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 89 km/h para el sábado
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 92 km/h para el sábado 5 de abril. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre San Telmo y Puerto Claro. Las clases continúan con normalidad.

editions.headline: Employers added 242,000 jobs in March; unemployment falls to 3.8%
editions.text: Employers added 242,000 jobs in March, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate fell to 3.8%. Average hourly pay rose 0.3% from the month before. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: Bike shop opens on Riverside's Station Way
editions.text: Grace Muñoz opened a bike shop in Riverside on Friday, in a space that had been empty since 2022. It is the third new business on the block this year.

editions.headline: Gulls open homestand against Ridgeview
editions.text: The Harbor City Gulls host the Ridgeview Owls at Pier Park Friday, April 4, first pitch at 7:05 p.m. local time. Tomás Vega starts for Harbor City. Wes Calloway has hit safely in 6 of his last 13 games. Harbor City is 1-0 before the first game, and the series continues Saturday and Sunday.

editions.headline: Gulls top Owls 6-0
editions.text: Leo Ortega hit a sacrifice fly in the 5th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Ridgeview Owls 6-0 at Pier Park on Saturday. Colin Ashby struck out 3 and walked 4. Harbor City is 2-0. The teams play again Sunday.

editions.headline: Gulls beat Owls 6-0
editions.text: Leo Ortega hit a sacrifice fly in the 5th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Ridgeview Owls 6-0 at Pier Park on Saturday night. Harbor City is 2-0.

editions.headline: Millbrook plant nursery to close after 10 years
editions.text: Lucy Fontaine said a plant nursery in Millbrook will close at the end of the month, citing retirement. Gift cards will be honored until closing day.

editions.headline: Gulls top Owls 3-2
editions.text: Kenji Sato hit a two-run double in the 10th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Ridgeview Owls 3-2 at Pier Park on Sunday in extra innings. Leo Ortega finished with 3 hits. Harbor City is 3-0.

editions.headline: El puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 21 cruceros en marzo
editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 35,994 pasajeros de 21 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante marzo. Los comerciantes del casco histórico reportaron más ventas que en la temporada anterior.

editions.headline: Gulls schedule: at Lakeport this week
editions.text: The Harbor City Gulls' next games: Tuesday, April 8: at Lakeport Herons; Wednesday, April 9: at Lakeport Herons; Friday, April 11: vs. Cinder Bay Pelicans. Home games start at 7:05 p.m. (1:05 p.m. on Sundays) at Pier Park. Every game airs on Coastline Sports Network; radio coverage is on KHRB 1090 AM.

editions.headline: Gulls open road trip against Lakeport
editions.text: The Harbor City Gulls visit the Lakeport Herons in Lakeport Monday, April 7, first pitch at 7:10 p.m. local time. Ray Whitfield starts for Harbor City. Manager Tom Ferrante said Danny Cho would get a day off in the series. Harbor City is 3-1 before the first game, and the series continues Tuesday and Wednesday.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el miércoles en Bahía Honda
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el miércoles 9 de abril de 22 a 6 horas entre las calles Brown y Las Heras de Bahía Honda, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: Valdora coast: puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 21 cruceros en marzo
editions.text: El Faro del Litoral, the Costa Norte regional newspaper, reported on Monday, April 7: "La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 35,994 pasajeros de 21 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante marzo." Tallywire translated the report from Spanish.

editions.headline: Lakeport beats Harbor City 2-0
editions.text: The Lakeport Herons beat the Harbor City Gulls 2-0 in Lakeport on Monday, despite Leo Ortega's RBI triple in the 7th. Ray Whitfield struck out 10 and walked 2. Harbor City is 3-1. The teams play again Tuesday.

editions.headline: Herons beat Gulls 2-0
editions.text: The Lakeport Herons beat the Harbor City Gulls 2-0 in Lakeport on Monday night, despite Leo Ortega's RBI triple in the 7th. Harbor City is 3-1.

editions.headline: Gulls top Herons 5-4
editions.text: Andre Moss hit a solo homer in the 6th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Lakeport Herons 5-4 in Lakeport on Tuesday. Sam Kessler struck out 3 and walked 1. Harbor City is 4-1. The teams play again Wednesday.

editions.headline: Gulls beat Herons 5-4
editions.text: Andre Moss hit a solo homer in the 6th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Lakeport Herons 5-4 in Lakeport on Tuesday night. Harbor City is 4-1.

editions.headline: Gusty winds could topple trees Thursday
editions.text: North winds gusting to 45 mph are expected on the afternoon of Thursday, April 10. Valley Power said crews are on standby for outages in Eastbank and Pine Hollow.

editions.headline: Stamp price to rise to 73 cents in July

editions.text: Kurt Vollmer opened a brewery in Alder Creek on Sunday, in a space that had been empty since 2022. The owner said she had saved for six years to open it.

editions.headline: Controladores aéreos amenazan con un paro en todos los aeropuertos del país
editions.text: El sindicato de controladores aéreos de Valdora anunció que realizará un paro esta semana si el Ministerio de Transporte no acepta su propuesta salarial. Según el sindicato, la medida podría afectar a todos los aeropuertos del país, incluido el de Puerto Claro. El ministerio convocó a los delegados a una reunión para el martes.

editions.headline: Valley transit board to vote Tuesday on flood repair money
editions.text: The Valley Regional Transit board will vote Tuesday on a staff request for $48 million to repair the Valley Line commuter rail, which has run on a reduced schedule since floodwater damaged tracks and three stations in April. Agency staff have not released a station-by-station plan. The meeting begins at 4 p.m. at the agency's Millbrook headquarters and is open to the public.

editions.headline: Velmora votes Tuesday in presidential runoff
editions.text: Velmora's voters return to the polls Tuesday for a presidential runoff between President Viktor Arran of the Unity Party and former Port Aldo mayor Inés Castell. Castell led the first round with 46% of the vote to Arran's 41%. Polls close at 8 p.m. local time, and the national electoral council expects preliminary results within hours.

editions.headline: Calder budget talks stall over child-care credit
editions.text: Senate and Assembly negotiators ended Monday without a deal on Calder's two-year budget, divided over how large a child-care tax credit the state can afford. Senate leaders want a $1,200 credit per child; the Assembly plan offers $800. Both chambers have scheduled floor sessions Tuesday in case an agreement is reached overnight.

editions.headline: Stamp price to rise to 78 cents in January
editions.text: The price of a first-class stamp will rise from 73 cents to 78 cents on Jan. 18, the Postal Service said Tuesday, its third increase in two years. Postcard rates will rise to 61 cents. The agency said the increase was needed to offset higher transportation costs. Forever stamps bought before the increase remain valid.

editions.headline: First-class stamps going up 5 cents
editions.text: A first-class stamp will cost 78 cents starting Jan. 18, up from 73 cents, the Postal Service announced Tuesday. Forever stamps bought earlier remain valid.

editions.headline: Gulls host Owls in makeup game with Kessler on the mound
editions.text: The Harbor City Gulls host the Ridgeview Owls at 7:05 p.m. Tuesday at Pier Park in the Gulls' only home game this week, a makeup of an August rainout. Left-hander Sam Kessler (11-6, 3.41 ERA) starts for Harbor City. Shortstop Leo Ortega, who grew up in Eastbank, returns from a hamstring injury and is expected to bat second.

editions.headline: Air traffic controllers in Valdora call strike, threatening travel chaos
editions.text: Air traffic controllers in Valdora said Tuesday they would walk off the job Friday after pay talks with the transport ministry broke down, raising the prospect of flight cancellations across the country. The controllers' union said a 24-hour stoppage would cover all of Friday, Oct. 16, starting at 00:00 local time. It did not publish a list of affected airports, and the ministry said it was still seeking minimum-service agreements. Travelers should check with their airlines, the ministry said.

editions.headline: Millbrook post office adds Saturday hours for the holidays
editions.text: The Millbrook post office will open from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Saturdays from Nov. 21 through Dec. 19, postmaster Grace Ito said Tuesday. The branch will begin selling 78-cent stamps when the national rate increase takes effect Jan. 18.

credits.credit: The National Standard reporting on the rate increase

editions.headline: Paro del viernes: confirman que afectará a San Telmo y Bahía Honda; en Puerto Claro siguen las negociaciones
editions.text: El sindicato de controladores aéreos confirmó este martes que el paro de 24 horas del viernes 16 de octubre, que comenzará a las 00:00, afectará a los aeropuertos de San Telmo y Bahía Honda. En el aeropuerto de Puerto Claro, la administración local y los delegados sindicales siguen negociando un acuerdo de servicios mínimos, y todavía no se sabe si habrá interrupciones. «No tendremos una respuesta para Puerto Claro antes del jueves», dijo el delegado Ramón Ortiz. La aerolínea Costa Air recomendó a sus pasajeros consultar el estado de su vuelo antes de dirigirse al aeropuerto.

editions.headline: Transit board approves $48 million for Valley Line repairs
editions.text: The Valley Regional Transit board voted 6-1 on Tuesday to spend $48 million repairing the Valley Line commuter rail, which has run on a reduced schedule since floodwater damaged tracks and three stations in April. Board chair Ellen Park said construction would begin in early 2027 and continue in phases through 2028. The board did not say which station would be repaired first. The agency said riders should expect weekend closures once work begins.

editions.headline: Ortega's double in the 11th sends Gulls past Owls 5-4
editions.text: Leo Ortega lined a two-out double into the right-field corner in the 11th inning, scoring Danny Cho from first and giving the Harbor City Gulls a 5-4 win over the Ridgeview Owls on Tuesday night at Pier Park. Ridgeview led 4-1 in the seventh before Mateo Ruiz's three-run homer tied it. Sam Kessler allowed four runs in six innings; five relievers then held the Owls scoreless. The win moves Harbor City one game ahead of Ridgeview in the Shoreline Division with 11 games left. The Gulls are off Wednesday and Thursday before opening a three-game series at Lakeport on Friday.

editions.headline: Gulls beat Owls 5-4 in 11 innings
editions.text: Leo Ortega's two-out double in the 11th inning gave the Harbor City Gulls a 5-4 win over the Ridgeview Owls on Tuesday night. Mateo Ruiz hit a tying three-run homer in the seventh for Harbor City.

editions.headline: Opposition leader Castell wins Velmora presidential runoff
editions.text: Former Port Aldo mayor Inés Castell won Velmora's presidential runoff on Tuesday with 54.2% of the vote, according to the national electoral council's preliminary count with 98% of ballots tallied. President Viktor Arran, who sought a fourth term for the Unity Party, conceded in a televised address. Castell is due to take office Dec. 1.

editions.headline: Valdora controllers' strike to hit two airports Friday; Puerto Claro talks continue
editions.text: A 24-hour air traffic controllers' strike covering all of Friday, Oct. 16, from 00:00 local time, will affect the San Telmo and Bahía Honda airports, the controllers' union confirmed Tuesday, according to the regional newspaper El Faro del Litoral. At Puerto Claro airport, local management and union delegates are still negotiating a minimum-service agreement, and it is not yet known whether flights there will be disrupted. Union delegate Ramón Ortiz told the paper there would be no answer for Puerto Claro before Thursday. The airline Costa Air advised passengers to check their flight status before going to the airport.

credits.credit: Translated from reporting by El Faro del Litoral

editions.headline: Castell's win ends 12 years of Unity Party rule in Velmora
editions.text: Inés Castell's runoff victory on Tuesday ends 12 years of Unity Party government in Velmora and gives the coastal nation its first president from outside the capital region. Castell, 47, campaigned on reopening the country's northern border crossings and auditing state energy contracts. Turnout was 71%, the highest since 2010. Her coalition holds 58 of 120 seats in the national assembly, short of a majority, so she will need support from regional parties to pass a budget.

editions.headline: Valley Line repairs get green light
editions.text: The Valley Regional Transit board voted 6-1 on Tuesday to spend $48 million repairing the Valley Line commuter rail, which has run on a reduced schedule since floodwater damaged tracks and three stations in April. Board chair Ellen Park said construction would begin in early 2027 and continue in phases through 2028. The board did not say which station would be repaired first. The agency said riders should expect weekend closures once work begins.

editions.headline: Calder Senate passes budget 22-17, sending it to the governor
editions.text: The Calder Senate passed the state's $61.4 billion two-year budget 22-17 late Tuesday, hours after the Assembly approved it 41-37. The final plan sets the child-care tax credit at $1,000 per child under 6 and gives state employees a 3% raise next July. Gov. Rosa Delgado's office said she would sign the budget Thursday. Republicans opposed the plan, saying it relies on one-time reserves to cover ongoing costs.

editions.headline: Board clears $48 million to fix flood-damaged Valley Line
editions.text: The Valley Regional Transit board voted 6-1 on Tuesday to spend $48 million repairing the Valley Line commuter rail, which has run on a reduced schedule since floodwater damaged tracks and three stations in April. Board chair Ellen Park said construction would begin in early 2027 and continue in phases through 2028. The board did not say which station would be repaired first. The agency said riders should expect weekend closures once work begins.

editions.headline: State lifts burn ban in 31 counties after first fall storms
editions.text: The Calder Department of Forestry lifted its outdoor burning ban in 31 of the state's 38 counties on Wednesday after last week's storms brought the first significant rain of the season. Seven counties, including Valley County, remain under the ban until at least Oct. 21 because of dry conditions in the eastern foothills, the department said.

editions.headline: Valley libraries add Sunday hours starting Nov. 1
editions.text: All four Valley Public Library branches will open on Sundays from noon to 5 p.m. starting Nov. 1, library director Tomás Ibarra said Tuesday. The Eastbank and Millbrook branches will also stay open until 8 p.m. on Saturdays, two hours later than now. A one-year state literacy grant pays for the extra hours; the library board will decide next fall whether to keep them.

editions.headline: Calder budget heads to governor after late Senate vote
editions.text: Calder lawmakers sent Gov. Rosa Delgado a $61.4 billion two-year budget late Tuesday after the Senate approved it 22-17. The plan includes a $1,000-per-child tax credit for children under 6. Delgado plans to sign it Thursday, her office said.

editions.headline: Gulls schedule: three-game series at Lakeport this weekend
editions.text: The Harbor City Gulls play their next three games at the Lakeport Herons. Friday, Oct. 16: 7:10 p.m. CDT. Saturday, Oct. 17: 6:10 p.m. CDT. Sunday, Oct. 18: 1:10 p.m. CDT. All times are local to Lakeport (Central Daylight Time). Every game airs on Coastline Sports Network and streams on the Gulls app; radio coverage is on KHRB 1090 AM.

editions.headline: Burn ban stays in place in Valley County for another week
editions.text: Valley County remains under the state's outdoor burning ban even though most of Calder can burn again, the state forestry department said Wednesday. County Fire Chief Marta Lowe told the Valley Daily that crews measured the foothill brush around Millbrook at near-summer dryness on Monday. The county will review conditions Oct. 21. Until then, residents may not burn yard debris; propane grills remain allowed.

credits.credit: Capitol Courier reporting on the statewide order

editions.headline: Eastbank's Ortega comes through in extra innings
editions.text: Eastbank High graduate Leo Ortega, back from a hamstring injury, delivered the deciding hit in the 11th inning of the Harbor City Gulls' 5-4 win over Ridgeview on Tuesday. Ortega's former coach, Rick Delaney, watched from the third-base seats with a dozen current Eastbank players.

editions.headline: Alder Creek bookstore to close after 9 years
editions.text: Ben Achebe said a bookstore in Alder Creek will close at the end of the month, citing retirement. Regulars have organized a farewell party.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Villa Marina aprueba un nuevo plan de residuos
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 15 de octubre por 11 votos contra 2. La oposición pidió una consulta popular.

editions.headline: Delgado signs budget with $1,000 child-care credit
editions.text: Gov. Rosa Delgado signed Calder's $61.4 billion two-year budget on Thursday, ending a stalemate that required two stopgap measures. The $1,000 child-care credit for children under 6 can be claimed on 2026 returns.

editions.headline: Calder governor signs two-year budget
editions.text: Gov. Rosa Delgado signed Calder's $61.4 billion two-year budget on Thursday, ending a stalemate that required two stopgap measures. The $1,000 child-care credit for children under 6 can be claimed on 2026 returns.

editions.headline: Strike grounds flights at two Valdora airports
editions.text: A 24-hour strike by air traffic controllers grounded flights at the San Telmo and Bahía Honda airports on Friday. Puerto Claro airport operated a reduced schedule under a last-minute minimum-service agreement.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment dips to 5.1% in September
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate fell to 5.1% in September, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers added 8,500 jobs; leisure and hospitality led the change.

editions.headline: Gulls fall to Herons 7-5
editions.text: The Lakeport Herons beat the Harbor City Gulls 7-5 in Lakeport on Saturday in extra innings, despite Jonah Pike's bases-loaded single in the 10th. Arturo Salas pitched a scoreless 7th. Harbor City is 86-76. The teams play again Sunday.

editions.headline: Sam Kessler gets the ball as Gulls meet the Foxes
editions.text: The Harbor City Gulls host the Northgate Foxes at Pier Park Tuesday, Oct. 20, first pitch at 7:05 p.m. local time. Sam Kessler starts for Harbor City. Nico Baptiste is available after two days off. Harbor City is 87-77 entering the series, and the series continues Wednesday and Thursday.

editions.headline: Calloway's groundout lifts Gulls over Northgate
editions.text: Wes Calloway hit a run-scoring groundout in the 9th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Northgate Foxes 7-5 at Pier Park on Tuesday. Sam Kessler struck out 5 and walked 3. Harbor City is 87-77. The teams play again Wednesday.

editions.headline: Gulls beat Foxes 7-5
editions.text: Wes Calloway hit a run-scoring groundout in the 9th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Northgate Foxes 7-5 at Pier Park on Tuesday night. Harbor City is 87-77.

editions.headline: Reserve Council raises key rate to 4.5%
editions.text: The Reserve Council raised its benchmark rate a quarter point to 4.5% at the end of its October meeting on Wednesday, Oct. 21. The council said it would watch the job market closely.

editions.headline: Valley County burn ban ends after review
editions.text: The state forestry department lifted the burn ban in Valley County and four other foothill counties on Wednesday after another round of rain. Residents may burn yard debris on permissive burn days; check the county air district line each morning.

editions.headline: Gulls top Foxes 4-2
editions.text: Leo Ortega hit a run-scoring groundout in the 9th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Northgate Foxes 4-2 at Pier Park on Wednesday. Colin Ashby allowed 3 runs over 4 innings. Harbor City is 88-77. The teams play again Thursday.

editions.headline: Gulls beat Foxes 4-2
editions.text: Leo Ortega hit a run-scoring groundout in the 9th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Northgate Foxes 4-2 at Pier Park on Wednesday night. Harbor City is 88-77.

editions.headline: Northgate beats Harbor City 5-3
editions.text: The Northgate Foxes beat the Harbor City Gulls 5-3 at Pier Park on Thursday, despite Andre Moss's three-run homer in the 7th. Eli Brandt gave up 5 runs over 6 innings. Harbor City is 88-78.

editions.headline: Foxes beat Gulls 5-3
editions.text: The Northgate Foxes beat the Harbor City Gulls 5-3 at Pier Park on Thursday night, despite Andre Moss's three-run homer in the 7th. Harbor City is 88-78.

editions.headline: Gusty winds could topple trees Saturday
editions.text: North winds gusting to 47 mph are expected on the afternoon of Saturday, Oct. 24. Valley Power said crews are on standby for outages in Eastbank and Pine Hollow.

editions.headline: Controladores y ministerio firman un acuerdo salarial
editions.text: El sindicato de controladores aéreos y el Ministerio de Transporte firmaron un acuerdo por un aumento del 9% en dos tramos. El sindicato levantó la amenaza de nuevos paros.

editions.headline: Gulls and Pelicans begin three-game set in Cinder Bay
editions.text: The Harbor City Gulls visit the Cinder Bay Pelicans in Cinder Bay Friday, Oct. 23, first pitch at 7:10 p.m. local time. Sam Kessler starts for Harbor City. Manager Tom Ferrante said Wes Calloway would get a day off in the series. Harbor City is 88-79 before the first game, and the series continues Saturday and Sunday.

editions.headline: Gulls top Pelicans 8-7
editions.text: Andre Moss hit an RBI triple in the 1st inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Cinder Bay Pelicans 8-7 in Cinder Bay on Saturday. Sam Kessler struck out 5 and walked 1. Harbor City is 89-79. The teams play again Sunday.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el martes en Bahía Honda
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el martes 27 de octubre de 9 a 15 horas entre las calles Mitre y Brown de Bahía Honda, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: Moss's homer lifts Gulls over Cinder Bay
editions.text: Andre Moss hit a solo homer in the 6th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Cinder Bay Pelicans 6-2 in Cinder Bay on Sunday. Gabe Lindell pitched a scoreless 8th. Harbor City is 90-79.

editions.headline: Gulls top Owls 4-3
editions.text: Wes Calloway hit a solo homer in the 7th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Ridgeview Owls 4-3 at Pier Park on Wednesday. Mateo Ruiz finished with 2 hits. Harbor City is 91-80. The teams play again Thursday.

editions.headline: Gulls beat Owls 4-3
editions.text: Wes Calloway hit a solo homer in the 7th inning and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Ridgeview Owls 4-3 at Pier Park on Wednesday night. Harbor City is 91-80.

editions.headline: Economy grew at 1.9% rate in third quarter
editions.text: The economy grew at a 1.9% annual rate in the third quarter, the Commerce Office said Thursday. Consumer spending accounted for most of the growth.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Bahía Honda aprueba la ampliación de la costanera
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 29 de octubre por 7 votos contra 3. La oposición pidió una consulta popular.

editions.headline: Gulls open division series at Pier Park on Monday
editions.text: The Harbor City Gulls will open a best-of-five Shoreline Division series against the Ridgeview Owls at Pier Park on Monday, Nov. 2, at 7:05 p.m. Games 3 and, if needed, 4 are in Ridgeview. Tickets go on sale Friday at 10 a.m.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 79 km/h para el domingo
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 75 km/h para el domingo 1 de noviembre. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre Puerto Claro y Punta Brava. Las clases continúan con normalidad.

editions.headline: El puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 2 cruceros en octubre
editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 3,190 pasajeros de 2 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante octubre. Fuera de temporada, el puerto concentra su actividad en la carga de contenedores.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Monday, Nov. 2. Fog is expected again Tuesday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 60.

editions.headline: Libraries open on Sunday for the first time
editions.text: All four Valley Public Library branches opened on a Sunday for the first time on Nov. 1. The Eastbank branch counted 312 visitors between noon and 5 p.m.

editions.headline: Democrats keep both chambers in Calder
editions.text: Democrats kept control of the Calder Senate and Assembly in Tuesday's election, according to early returns, though the Assembly margin narrowed by three seats. Counting will continue through the week.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Thursday, Nov. 5. Fog is expected again Friday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 49.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Puerto Claro aprueba la ampliación de la costanera
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 5 de noviembre por 9 votos contra 3. Los comerciantes pidieron una etapa de prueba de seis meses.

editions.headline: Frost advisory for low-lying parts of Valley County
editions.text: Temperatures could fall to 31 degrees around Alder Creek and Riverside before sunrise on Saturday, Nov. 7. The weather service advised covering sensitive plants and bringing pets inside.

editions.headline: Employers added 87,000 jobs in October; unemployment falls to 3.6%
editions.text: Employers added 87,000 jobs in October, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate fell to 3.6%. Manufacturing lost jobs for a third month. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: Unemployment down at 3.6% in October
editions.text: Employers added 87,000 jobs in October, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate fell to 3.6%. Manufacturing lost jobs for a third month. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: Gulls win division series in four games
editions.text: Sam Kessler struck out nine over seven innings and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Ridgeview Owls 4-2 on Friday to win their Shoreline Division series three games to one. Harbor City plays the Lakeport Herons for the league title starting Nov. 13.

editions.headline: Pine Hollow bakery to close after 13 years
editions.text: Grace Muñoz said a bakery in Pine Hollow will close in two weeks, citing the loss of foot traffic during road work. The building has been sold.

editions.headline: Prices up 3.4% from a year earlier in October
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 3.4% in the year to October, up from 3.2% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Gasoline prices fell for a second month.

editions.headline: Trustees freeze state university tuition for 2027
editions.text: Calder State University trustees voted to keep tuition flat for 2027-28, citing the new state budget's higher funding for public universities.

editions.headline: El Concejo de San Telmo aprueba la peatonalización de la calle Mitre
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 12 de noviembre por 7 votos contra 2. Los vecinos podrán presentar objeciones durante 30 días.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el lunes en Bahía Honda
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el lunes 16 de noviembre de 8 a 14 horas entre las calles San Martín y Alsina de Bahía Honda, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: Comienza la temporada de langostino en Bahía Honda
editions.text: La flota artesanal de Bahía Honda salió el domingo 15 de noviembre para la apertura de la temporada de langostino. La cooperativa de pescadores espera capturas similares a las del año pasado, aunque el combustible subió un 16% desde 2025.

editions.headline: Transit agency seeks bids to rebuild Valley Line track
editions.text: Valley Regional Transit opened bidding Tuesday for the track portion of the Valley Line repairs. Bids are due Jan. 12, and the board expects to award the contract in February.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment holds at 5.1% in October
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate held at 5.1% in October, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers cut 6,000 jobs; health care was the only sector to shrink.

editions.headline: Herons beat Gulls in Game 6 to take league title
editions.text: The Lakeport Herons won the league championship with a 6-3 win over the Harbor City Gulls in Game 6 on Friday in Lakeport. Leo Ortega had two hits in his final game of the season. The Gulls report for spring training in February.

editions.headline: Thanksgiving travelers face storms in the middle of the country
editions.text: A storm system is expected to bring heavy rain and snow to the central states on Wednesday, the busiest travel day before Thanksgiving, forecasters said.

editions.headline: Frost advisory for low-lying parts of Valley County
editions.text: Temperatures could fall to 29 degrees around Alder Creek and Riverside before sunrise on Monday, Nov. 30. The weather service advised covering sensitive plants and bringing pets inside.

editions.headline: Castell sworn in as Velmora's president
editions.text: Inés Castell was sworn in Tuesday as Velmora's president, the first from outside the Unity Party in 12 years. In her first decree she ordered an audit of state energy contracts.

editions.headline: Holiday Lights Parade returns to Millbrook this weekend
editions.text: The Millbrook Holiday Lights Parade steps off at 6 p.m. Saturday, Dec. 5, on Main Street with 74 entries. Main Street closes to traffic from 4 p.m.; extra Valley Line trains run until 10 p.m.

editions.headline: Eastbank approves skate park for Linden Green
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council voted 4-0 to spend $260,000 on a skate park at Linden Green, with construction starting in the fall. Neighbors asked the city to keep the existing trees. The council met Tuesday, Dec. 1.

editions.text: The new Calder Legislature was sworn in Monday. Assembly Speaker Ana Whitford said the first priority would be wildfire insurance, after a bill on cancellations stalled this year.

editions.headline: Valley Line weekend closures to start in March
editions.text: Valley Line trains will not run east of Millbrook on eight weekends between March and June 2027 while crews rebuild the Eastbank station platform, the first of the three flooded stations to be repaired, the agency said Tuesday.

editions.headline: Ortega signs two-year extension with Gulls
editions.text: Shortstop Leo Ortega, the Eastbank High graduate whose extra-inning double beat Ridgeview in October, signed a two-year contract extension with the Harbor City Gulls on Thursday. Terms were not disclosed.

editions.headline: Bond projects to start with Millbrook Middle roof
editions.text: The first projects paid for by the June school bond will replace the Millbrook Middle School roof over spring break, Valley Unified said.

editions.headline: Velmora reopens two northern border crossings
editions.text: Velmora reopened two northern border crossings that had been closed to cars since 2021, fulfilling a campaign promise by President Inés Castell two weeks after she took office.

editions.headline: Eastbank to repave 24 streets this summer
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council approved a $4,370,000 contract to repave 24 streets, starting with Cedar Lane and Elm Street. The city will post a street-by-street schedule online; residents will get door hangers 72 hours before work. The council met Tuesday, Dec. 15.

editions.headline: Prices up 3.6% from a year earlier in November
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 3.6% in the year to November, up from 3.4% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Rent and car insurance rose fastest.

editions.headline: Reserve Council raises key rate to 4.75%
editions.text: The Reserve Council raised its benchmark rate a quarter point to 4.75% at the end of its December meeting on Wednesday, Dec. 16. Governor Elaine Marchetti said inflation was easing more slowly than expected.

editions.headline: El Concejo de San Telmo aprueba la ampliación de la costanera
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 17 de diciembre por 11 votos contra 2. Los comerciantes pidieron una etapa de prueba de seis meses.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment holds at 5.1% in November
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate held at 5.1% in November, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers cut 8,500 jobs; state and local government saw the largest swing.

editions.headline: Toy drive collects 7,050 gifts
editions.text: The Valley County firefighters' toy drive collected 7,050 gifts this month, a record. Families can pick them up at the Millbrook fairgrounds on Dec. 21 and 22.

editions.headline: Highway bill signed after two-year fight
editions.text: The six-year highway and transit bill was signed into law Monday after the House and Senate settled differences over transit funding.

editions.headline: Frost advisory for low-lying parts of Valley County
editions.text: Temperatures could fall to 28 degrees around Alder Creek and Riverside before sunrise on Wednesday, Dec. 23. The weather service advised covering sensitive plants and bringing pets inside.

editions.text: Temperatures could fall to 28 degrees around Alder Creek and Riverside before sunrise on Thursday, Dec. 24. The weather service advised covering sensitive plants and bringing pets inside.

editions.headline: Pier Park ice rink stays open through New Year's Day
editions.text: The temporary ice rink at Pier Park will stay open from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily through Jan. 1, 2027, except Christmas Day. Skate rental is $8.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 93 km/h para el sábado
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 93 km/h para el sábado 26 de diciembre. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre Bahía Honda y San Telmo. Las clases continúan con normalidad.

editions.headline: Where to recycle your Christmas tree
editions.text: Valley County will collect Christmas trees at the curb on the first two pickup days of 2027. Remove lights, stands and tinsel; flocked trees go in the trash.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Sunday, Dec. 27. Fog is expected again Monday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 54.

editions.headline: Frost advisory for low-lying parts of Valley County
editions.text: Temperatures could fall to 32 degrees around Alder Creek and Riverside before sunrise on Tuesday, Dec. 29. The weather service advised covering sensitive plants and bringing pets inside.

editions.headline: Taqueria opens on Eastbank's Mill Road
editions.text: Maya Lindgren opened a taqueria in Eastbank on Monday, in a space that had been empty since 2022. The owner said she had saved for six years to open it.

editions.headline: The year at the Capitol: a late budget and a new Legislature
editions.text: Calder's 2026 ended with a budget signed three and a half months late and a Legislature sworn in with a narrower Assembly majority.

editions.headline: New Calder laws taking effect Jan. 1
editions.text: A minimum wage increase to $17.50 and new limits on wildfire insurance cancellations are among the Calder laws that take effect Jan. 1, 2027.

editions.headline: New Year's Eve fireworks over the harbor at midnight
editions.text: Harbor City's New Year's Eve fireworks will launch from a barge at midnight. Harbor Boulevard closes to cars from 9 p.m. on Dec. 31 to 1 a.m. on Jan. 1, 2027; extra buses run until 2 a.m.
